excerpt:
SAMPLE — NOT A REAL FILING
United States District Court, [Sample Jurisdiction]

ARGUMENT

I. Historical cell-site location information is a Fourth Amendment search.

The Fourth Amendment protects people, not places. Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347 (1967). Long-term GPS monitoring of a vehicle is a search. United States v. Jones, 565 U.S. 400 (2012). A warrant is required to search the digital contents of a cell phone incident to arrest. Riley v. California, 573 U.S. 373 (2014).

Applying those principles, the Government's acquisition of seven days or more of historical cell-site records is a Fourth Amendment search; police generally must obtain a warrant supported by probable cause. Carpenter v. United States, 585 U.S. 946 (2018). The Court declined to extend the third-party doctrine of Smith v. Maryland, 442 U.S. 735 (1979), to that category of cell-site records.

The court of appeals had affirmed the denial of suppression. United States v. Carpenter, 819 F.3d 880 (6th Cir. 2016). That disposition does not control after the Supreme Court's decision.
